Subpages At The Stonebridge School, our core curriculum provides strong foundations in English, Mathematics and Science.

By the time children leave The Stonebridge School, we want them to have secure foundations in English, Mathematics and Science, and the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for the next stage of their education.
Maths Subject Lead: Gabriella Ortutai Our Mathematics curriculum develops children’s fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills and supports them to become confident and successful mathematicians.
Reading Subject Lead: Preesha Lachani Our Reading curriculum develops children’s fluency, vocabulary, comprehension and enjoyment of reading.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission, Vision and Values - The Stonebridge School
pageCache.text:
Mission, Vision and Values
To nurture every child and ensure excellence and equity for all.
Our mission brings together our commitment to the whole child with high expectations. We want every child to feel known, valued and supported, whilst ensuring all pupils have what they need to achieve excellence.
A thriving, ambitious community where every child feels they belong, is inspired to succeed and develops the confidence to thrive in an ever-changing wider world.
Our vision reflects our aspiration for children not only to succeed academically, but to develop the confidence, character and sense of belonging they need for their next steps and future lives.
Our six values are taught across the year, with each chosen to reflect the journey our children experience through the school year.
Courage
Be brave. Have a go. Embrace new challenges.
The beginning of a new school year brings change, new relationships and new learning. We encourage children to have the courage to try, take positive risks and believe in themselves.
Kindness
Care for others. Include everyone. Make a difference.
As our school community grows together, we deepen children’s understanding of empathy, compassion and belonging. Kindness brings the nurture in our mission to life.
Responsibility
Own your choices. Take charge of your learning.
A new term brings a fresh start. Children learn to take increasing responsibility for their choices, behaviour, learning and contribution to their community.
Respect
Value yourself. Value others. Value our community.
Children learn that respect means valuing themselves and others, appreciating difference and treating everyone with dignity and fairness, supporting our commitment to equity and belonging.
Ambition
Aim high. Work hard. Be your best.
At a key point in the academic year, we reinforce high expectations and the belief that every child can achieve. Ambition reflects the excellence at the heart of our mission.
Resilience
Keep going. Learn from challenges. Finish strong.
As children reach the end of the year and prepare for transition, resilience reminds them to persevere, learn from setbacks and approach their next steps positively.
Our journey through each academic year:
We begin with the courage to start, build our community through kindness, take responsibility for ourselves and our learning, show respect for ourselves and others, develop the ambition to aim high, and finish with the resilience to keep going.
Together, our mission, vision and values express what we want for every child: to be nurtured, to belong, to achieve excellence and to develop the character and confidence to thrive beyond our school.

Wraparound Care
We are pleased to offer wraparound childcare for families before and after the school day.
Our Breakfast Club and After-School Club are provided by Kidzplay-Afterschool Club, the organisation currently providing wraparound childcare services at Stonebridge.
The club provides childcare for children aged 4 to 11 years and is registered with Ofsted. It provides a safe, welcoming and enjoyable environment where children can relax, play and take part in a range of activities outside normal school hours.
The After-School Club operates from 3.00pm to 6.00pm on weekdays. Kidzplay-Afterschool Club also offers holiday childcare from 8.00am to 6.00pm during school holidays.

At The Stonebridge School, our core curriculum provides strong foundations in English, Mathematics and Science. We aim to develop secure knowledge, understanding and skills that children can build upon throughout their education.
Learning is carefully sequenced so that children build on what they already know. Key knowledge, vocabulary and skills are introduced, revisited and developed over time, enabling children to become increasingly confident and independent learners.
Teachers use assessment to identify what children know and understand, address misconceptions and plan appropriate next steps.
Our core curriculum is ambitious and accessible for all children. Teachers know their pupils well and make appropriate adaptations to teaching so that all children, including those with SEND and those who may face barriers to learning, can access the curriculum, develop secure knowledge and make progress.
Assessment is used to identify what children know and understand, address misconceptions and inform future teaching. Appropriate support and challenge are provided while maintaining high expectations for every child.
By the time children leave The Stonebridge School, we want them to have secure foundations in English, Mathematics and Science, and the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for the next stage of their education.
Phonics
Subject Lead: Abigail Foulkes-Murray
We use Read Write Inc. Phonics (RWI) as our systematic synthetic phonics programme.
Children are taught to recognise sounds and the letters that represent them, blend sounds to read words and segment words to support accurate spelling. They read books that are closely matched to their developing phonic knowledge, enabling them to practise their learning and develop accuracy, fluency and confidence.
Children’s progress is assessed regularly so that teaching is closely matched to their stage of development. Where children require additional support, targeted teaching is provided to help them develop secure phonic knowledge and become confident, independent readers.
Reading
Subject Lead: Preesha Lachani
Our Reading curriculum develops children’s fluency, vocabulary, comprehension and enjoyment of reading.
In Key Stage 1, VIPERS is used to support the explicit teaching of reading comprehension skills. Children develop their ability to explore vocabulary, infer meaning, predict, explain, retrieve information and sequence what they have read. An overview of the structure can be viewed HERE.
In Key Stage 2, Accelerated Reader is used to support independent reading. It enables children to engage with appropriately challenging books, read regularly and develop positive reading habits.
Please click HERE to view our whole-school Reading progression Map.
Children encounter a broad range of high-quality fiction, non-fiction and poetry. Through reading and discussion, they develop their understanding of texts, broaden their vocabulary and build the knowledge required to become confident and thoughtful readers.
Writing
Subject Lead: Humaira Masud
Our Writing curriculum develops children’s ability to communicate clearly, accurately and effectively for a range of purposes and audiences.
We use Literacy Tree to support the teaching of Writing. High-quality texts provide meaningful contexts for learning and expose children to a rich range of vocabulary, authors, genres and writing styles.
Our Writing overview can be viewed HERE.
Children develop their knowledge of composition, spelling, handwriting, vocabulary, grammar and punctuation. They are taught to plan, draft, evaluate and improve their writing and are given opportunities to apply their knowledge with increasing independence.
Spoken language and vocabulary development are embedded throughout the curriculum, enabling children to articulate their ideas and develop the language they need to communicate effectively.
Maths
Subject Lead: Gabriella Ortutai
Our Mathematics curriculum develops children’s fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills and supports them to become confident and successful mathematicians.
We use Ark Curriculum Plus Mathematics Mastery across all year groups, alongside other carefully selected resources to support teaching and learning.
Please click HERE to view the curriculum maps for all year groups.
Learning is carefully sequenced so that new mathematical knowledge builds on secure prior understanding. Children develop conceptual understanding alongside mathematical fluency and learn to make connections between different areas of mathematics.
Children are given regular opportunities to reason mathematically, solve problems and explain and justify their thinking using appropriate mathematical language. Teachers use assessment to identify misconceptions and adapt teaching so that children receive appropriate support and challenge.
The Mathematics curriculum provides coverage of the National Curriculum programmes of study and supports children to develop fluency, mathematical reasoning and problem-solving skills.
Science
Subject Lead: Ilwad Mohamed
Our Science curriculum develops children’s curiosity about the world and their understanding of scientific ideas and processes.
We use the Cornerstones Curriculum to support the teaching of Science. It provides a clear framework for progression, aligned with the National Curriculum, alongside high-quality resources to support teaching and learning.
The curriculum is structured so that important knowledge, concepts, vocabulary and subject-specific skills are introduced and developed over time. Learning builds on what has come before and prepares children for increasingly challenging content as they move through the school.
Children build substantive scientific knowledge alongside the disciplinary knowledge needed to think and work scientifically. Projects are sequenced to support the development of knowledge and vocabulary, with opportunities for first-hand observation and investigation where appropriate.
Across the primary years, children develop their understanding of areas including living things, plants, animals including humans, materials, forces, light, sound, electricity, Earth and space, evolution and inheritance. The scheme provides complete coverage of the National Curriculum programmes of study.
At The Stonebridge School, the Cornerstones framework supports our curriculum, whilst our teachers bring learning to life. They use their professional knowledge of their pupils to make learning meaningful, accessible and responsive to the needs of their classes.
The Cornerstones Science projects can be found in the wider curriculum document.

Attendance
Every day matters at The Stonebridge School
At The Stonebridge School, we want every child to feel that they belong, that they matter and that they are an important part of our school community.
Coming to school every day gives children opportunities to learn, build friendships, develop confidence and take part fully in school life.
We know that there can sometimes be reasons why coming to school is difficult. If your child is finding attendance or punctuality difficult, please talk to us early. We will listen, seek to understand what is happening and work with you and your child to find ways to help.
Being on time helps children to have a calm and positive start to the day, settle with their friends and be ready to learn.
8:35am – gates open8:50am – gates close8:55am – morning register closes
Children should arrive between 8:35am and 8:50am.
If your child arrives after the gates have closed, they will need to follow our late-arrival procedure. Children arriving after 8:55am will be recorded as arriving after the register has closed.
Regular lateness can mean missing important routines and learning at the beginning of the day. If getting to school on time is becoming difficult, please speak to us. We are here to help.
If your child is unable to attend school, please telephone us by 8:55am on 020 8965 6965.
Please call us on the first day of absence and on each following day unless another arrangement has been agreed with the school.
- your child's name and class- the reason they are absent- when you expect them to return, if known
If your child is expected at school and we have not heard from you, we will contact you as part of our attendance and safeguarding procedures.
Knowing where our children are is an important part of keeping them safe.
Every day at school matters.
Regular attendance helps children to:
- learn and make progress- build and maintain friendships- feel part of their class and school community- develop confidence, independence and positive routines- enjoy the wider opportunities and experiences of school life
Attendance is not simply about achieving a percentage. When children miss school, they can miss learning, friendships, experiences and opportunities that are not always easy to recreate.
There is also a clear relationship between attendance and achievement.
Department for Education research published in 2025 found that Year 6 pupils with 95–100% attendance were 1.3 times more likely to achieve the expected standard in reading, writing and maths than similar pupils attending 90–95% of the time, and 1.8 times more likely than similar pupils attending 85–90% of the time.
The research also found that missing 10 days of school in Year 6 was associated with around a 25% reduction in the likelihood of reaching the expected standard.
This is why every day really does matter.
We know that children become unwell and there will be times when your child needs to stay at home. We also know that it can sometimes be difficult to decide whether your child is well enough to come to school.
The NHS guidance ‘Is my child too ill for school?’ provides helpful advice about common childhood illnesses and whether children should attend school.
If you are unsure, please speak to us.
If your child has an ongoing physical or mental health need that is affecting their attendance, please let us know. We will work with you, your child and other professionals, where appropriate, to understand their needs and consider what support or reasonable adjustments may help.
Wherever possible, please arrange routine medical and dental appointments outside school hours.
We understand that this is not always possible, particularly for hospital or specialist appointments.
If your child needs to attend an appointment during the school day, please let us know in advance and provide evidence of the appointment if requested.
Where possible, children should come to school before their appointment and return afterwards so that they miss as little of their school day as possible.
Parents and carers should not expect holidays during term time to be authorised.
If you need to request any leave of absence during term time, whether your child will be travelling abroad or remaining in the UK, you must complete our online Leave of Absence Request Form in advance.
Complete the online Leave of Absence Request Form
Leave can only be granted by the school in accordance with the School Attendance Regulations. If you believe there are exceptional circumstances, please provide full details on the form so that your request can be considered.
Please complete the form and wait for the school's decision before making travel arrangements. Submitting a request does not mean that the absence has been authorised.
Unauthorised absence, including unauthorised term-time leave, may result in a referral to the Brent School Attendance Service and may lead to a penalty notice or other legal intervention in line with national legislation and Brent Council procedures.
Please see our Attendance Policy for full details.
We monitor attendance carefully so that we can identify concerns early and offer support.
If your child's attendance begins to fall, our first step will be to talk with you and understand what is happening. We will listen to you and your child, explore any barriers to attendance and work together to agree what may help.
Support might include practical changes, reasonable adjustments, an attendance support plan or working with other professionals and services, including the Brent School Attendance Service where appropriate.
Nationally, a child is considered persistently absent when they miss 10% or more of the school sessions available to them. We do not wait until a child reaches this point before offering help.
Where appropriate support has not been successful, has not been engaged with, or is not appropriate, formal or legal intervention may need to be considered in line with statutory guidance.
Attendance can sometimes be affected by SEND or additional needs, physical or mental health, anxiety, friendships, bereavement, family circumstances, housing difficulties or challenges with morning routines.
Every child and family is different. We will listen, seek to understand your child's individual circumstances and consider appropriate support and reasonable adjustments.
Please talk to us early if something is making it difficult for your child to attend regularly or arrive on time. You do not need to wait until attendance has become a serious concern before asking for help.
Call the School Office on 020 8965 6965 and ask to speak with Pastoral Lead Tracy Halpin, Headteacher Kate Pelazza or your child's class teacher.
We are here to listen and work with you.
Our approach to attendance reflects current Department for Education statutory guidance and research and our responsibilities as a maintained school.
